year old woman with memory loss "},"content":{"type":"html","$t":"\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;A 50 year old woman presented to our OPD with the complaints of\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELower back pain since the past 3 months\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EForgetfulness since 3 months\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESlurring of speech since 3 months\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe was born out of a non consanguinous marriage. She never attended school. She got married to a farmer when she was 16 years of age.\u0026nbsp; She had three normal vaginal deliveries (2 daughters and a son). She used to work as a farmer along with her husband.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E6 years back when she was working at a paddy field, she came in contact with electric shock for which she was admitted for 2 days in a local hospital. She had no complaints back then except for generalized weakness. She was given IV fluids during her hospital stay. She stopped going to work after this incident.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1.5 years back she again came in contact with electric shock when she was working at her house.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3 months back when she was walking to the washroom , she had a fall and injured her lower back. Ever since then she has been\u0026nbsp; complaining of lower back pain.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer daughter\u0026nbsp; tells us that her mother has been experiencing frequent falls since the past 3 months.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe also tells us that she previously used to be a very friendly person, who maintained good relations with their neighbor's, relatives. She would often worry regarding their financial situation and would frequently quarrel with her husband regarding starting their own business. Her daughter also told us that when her brother decided to move out with his wife, his mother was against it and ever since he moved out she has been low.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOver the past 3 months, her daughter reports that her mother has gradually stopped\u0026nbsp; interacting with others. She doesn't like meeting her relatives, friends. She also frequently has anger outbursts with no triggers\u0026nbsp; where she starts yelling but there are\u0026nbsp; no reports of\u0026nbsp; throwing objects in anger. She also tells that she would randomly start crying without any reason.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe reports that since the last month she is unable to recognize her relatives or neighbours. She only recognizes her family members. Her daughter also tells us that she occasionally passes urine and stools in her clothes and when scolded she starts crying.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHer daughter also reports that she now doesn't know her way home without proper guidance.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe used to previously cook for her family but now she isn't able to cook. She is unable to eat on her own, take shower or get dressed without help. She is unable to perform her routine daily activities without any help.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E20 days back, she had one episode of seizure which lasted for 15 minutes, consisted of tonic posturing of all her limb, uprolling of eyes, froth discharge from mouth which was followed by post-ictal confusion which lasted for 20 minutes. She had a similar episode 1 week back\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe is a thin built woman\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPallor +\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELack of facial expressions while conversing\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOn nervous system examination:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERight handedness\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EShe did not attend school\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHigher mental functions:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERight handedness\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMMSE: However Alzheimer's disease is a gradually progressive disease whereas lewy body dementia is of rapid onset. Vascular dementia is of sudden onset with focal neurological deficits. In lewy body dementia patients usually present with fluctuating memory \u0026amp; hallucinations, In frontotemporal dementia patients behaviour \u0026amp; execution is affected. So lets further go into details of dementia prior to coming to a diagnosis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEi5JhQ5TWaAAJi7Gn3rR484DysCCYfGzYyQ_nsoWaRPpQvJnwh4VHQaLoOnNBkpu5cNZe2l_qeRORXrp96XGA4af9QHNT3kveCP1DTMEwLidaEkovsevfUFM-FMG9rbqTs_4TCLrbGtuD9gp0zjlWJ-elbDO790q_LVE4wZrs7HsQyQYI-uNTkInPuHRw\/s1366\/Screenshot%20(196).png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"768\" data-original-width=\"1366\" height=\"360\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEi5JhQ5TWaAAJi7Gn3rR484DysCCYfGzYyQ_nsoWaRPpQvJnwh4VHQaLoOnNBkpu5cNZe2l_qeRORXrp96XGA4af9QHNT3kveCP1DTMEwLidaEkovsevfUFM-FMG9rbqTs_4TCLrbGtuD9gp0zjlWJ-elbDO790q_LVE4wZrs7HsQyQYI-uNTkInPuHRw\/w640-h360\/Screenshot%20(196).png\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESpeaker Notes:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThese are the learning objectives that you'll be able to take home after this presentation. First after a detailed history, we need to rule out pseudodementia and if it is a dementia is it cortical or subcortical and what are the lobes involved. We need to rule out the reversible cause of dementia before thinking about the irreversible causes.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgLkn9NxEEq8mA9rEUJID3WCF3GIUrvJGawbHPeRDHII0xEZRWVDiLicBwZ8bE3rkOlvoqd6ENXVk4NM6KOnrTt80q5f_Bem6fZ1bOqUh8V-SaoilpA8koPcmH0pZljMfVYzkgerhdWtuDoH-KLoFaNlTVUdXDxZK6BlI4kd9SEBa16968_QY_EvtYNNw\/s1366\/Screenshot%20(198).png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"768\" data-original-width=\"1366\" height=\"360\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgLkn9NxEEq8mA9rEUJID3WCF3GIUrvJGawbHPeRDHII0xEZRWVDiLicBwZ8bE3rkOlvoqd6ENXVk4NM6KOnrTt80q5f_Bem6fZ1bOqUh8V-SaoilpA8koPcmH0pZljMfVYzkgerhdWtuDoH-KLoFaNlTVUdXDxZK6BlI4kd9SEBa16968_QY_EvtYNNw\/w640-h360\/Screenshot%20(198).png\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESpeaker Notes:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESo what exactly is dementia and how would you define it by the DSM 5 (The diagnostic and statistical manual of mental disorders).\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EIt is the development of multiple cognitive defects including memory and one or more of the following cognitive domains :\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1. Complex attention\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E2. Executive function\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E3. Learning and Memory\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E4. Language\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E5. Motor or Social Cognition\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAnd also the decline of cognition noted by the clinician or the informant and also documented impairment in the patients cognition noted by a standardized neuropsychological testing.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe cognitive decline not explained by delirium or other mental disorders such as Schizophrenia or depressive disorder.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjdf8LFnL87yEplde1ckIDnvGARBoh87NPQIjZPCGHHzIeFvInlmS2O8HVsfw76qqhhhF--RpMoogW6VP1sZN-r0eHn9hgbBxw0QSyuNM0pimD6vrjTMCWUPEglYBgw3MONk_2G7YtuEI8sWUAzcZ_XHkfX2Lbz-rsr1oC_z9i_SsvgTBzj1CVvjPUV1w\/s1366\/Screenshot%20(199).png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"768\" data-original-width=\"1366\" height=\"360\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEjdf8LFnL87yEplde1ckIDnvGARBoh87NPQIjZPCGHHzIeFvInlmS2O8HVsfw76qqhhhF--RpMoogW6VP1sZN-r0eHn9hgbBxw0QSyuNM0pimD6vrjTMCWUPEglYBgw3MONk_2G7YtuEI8sWUAzcZ_XHkfX2Lbz-rsr1oC_z9i_SsvgTBzj1CVvjPUV1w\/w640-h360\/Screenshot%20(199).png\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESpeaker Notes:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESo what is the difference between Dementia and Pseudodementia? What is exactly pseudodementia?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPatients with pseudodementia have a rapid progression unlike the slow progression seen in dementia along with a more frequent psychiatry history and high suicidal tendencies. When asked\u0026nbsp; they would respond 'I do not know' or 'I do not want to answer' and they would have insight.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgBjFvkKMHcB-Vz5qeM1mBTcjqpHoV_HOVixfe3NRVioOtQcd_52Qcq08ebGbWQzjzCbIpGSQ8qQvqQ2S3DA47pskvVxJ8VDqrepkRdedwN0afOKrrkCYh9-dPn8cmnhJzKGf4TN9zE3gKF99OJ6ceinH6hubcsW-2cQdzXR0jGwIDIdDMtY126X3qqBA\/s1366\/image_2023-01-20_220406019.png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"768\" data-original-width=\"1366\" height=\"360\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEgBjFvkKMHcB-Vz5qeM1mBTcjqpHoV_HOVixfe3NRVioOtQcd_52Qcq08ebGbWQzjzCbIpGSQ8qQvqQ2S3DA47pskvVxJ8VDqrepkRdedwN0afOKrrkCYh9-dPn8cmnhJzKGf4TN9zE3gKF99OJ6ceinH6hubcsW-2cQdzXR0jGwIDIdDMtY126X3qqBA\/w640-h360\/image_2023-01-20_220406019.png\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESpeaker Notes:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESo before going into Dementia, i would like to talk briefly about memory and where it is stored.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThere are three types of memory, the immediate, recent (short term memory) and remote memory which is the long term memory.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe immediate memory is stored in the reticular activating system. Short term memory in the\u0026nbsp; hippocampus.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe long term memory could be explicit or non explicit. The explicit could be semantic - which includes information or knowledge stored in the cortical association areas or the episodic memory stored in the medial temporal.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EImplicit memory includes procedural skills, priming, conditioning.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; You can by the name understand what symptoms could be expected when each of this is involved.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EWhen the cortex is involved you would expect the patient to have - lack of insight, behavioral changes, aphasia, parietal lobar impairment with rarely involvement of the motor system. The subcortical dementia usually would have more motor complains.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEj-pe5E6skFQ1oTbVZYHpB2CxIfjn61SBAjrC911G9_xCXDEBS2oU4i5MO7mmRh1w2Y9S3u43SGldHV-R7kwEh_-vY3nKv5GC9s2GAvSdO0p2LFBwz5UCZ_B-sE3OK45D_icGAIzMMOWojlW-dpPvoqEibVoavzEbH6VF8Cifx2-MrztwYVU62fTPdWMg\/s1366\/Screenshot%20(203).png\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"768\" data-original-width=\"1366\" height=\"360\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEj-pe5E6skFQ1oTbVZYHpB2CxIfjn61SBAjrC911G9_xCXDEBS2oU4i5MO7mmRh1w2Y9S3u43SGldHV-R7kwEh_-vY3nKv5GC9s2GAvSdO0p2LFBwz5UCZ_B-sE3OK45D_icGAIzMMOWojlW-dpPvoqEibVoavzEbH6VF8Cifx2-MrztwYVU62fTPdWMg\/w640-h360\/Screenshot%20(203).png\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003EThis slide shows the individual lobar functions which would help us analyze which part of the brain is involved.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;\"\u003EFor example in our patient, his judgement, executive functions is impaired along with behavioral changes would point more towards the involvement of parietal lobe and the Frontal lobe. Patient with Frontotemporal dementia usually manifest with disinhibition, more of a behavioral changes, the patient would be unable to perform the Frontal lobar tests such as sequencing, planning.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAlzheimer's disease can be differentiated from parkinsions disease as it doesn't usually have motor symptoms.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003ESpeaker Notes:\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EUsing the KoreanService-Health Screening Database from 2009 to 2012, a total of 4 522 447 adults aged 60+ years without a history of dementia were analyzed and followed up for a mean of 5.4 years. Individuals were classified according to their baseline systolic BP (SBP) and diastolic BP; SBP 130 to \u0026lt;140 mm Hg and diastolic BP 80 to \u0026lt;90 mm Hg were used as reference groups. The risk of overall dementia and probable Alzheimer disease was significantly higher in the SBP≥160 and lower SBP groups.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EProbable AD and probable VaD occurred in 219 562 (4.8%) and 37 076 (0.8%) of participants, respectively\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDiabetes mellitus and risk of dementia: A meta-analysis of prospective observational studies\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe present meta-analysis of 28 observational studies showed a 73% increased risk of ATD, 56% increase in AD and 127% increase in VaD in patients with history of diabetes as compared with non-diabetic people.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEg3cF0CXYwDTn5utQSKfduKeKqL-Nic3ceJSYgLO0KOXGPotkX7-3X6Ekf5dmBYw6_JaYylEkn4S3wplZQ175tuh-sNbvy70EFSvKiQRDIvEcT5UhE7Co99X6PDU_j05FwA845jujHoZtRWCg3fTf2DyBqizgoTsGPFdVdWUnFhsXfE2CqAVODLuxDuFg\/s1366\/Screenshot%20(226).png\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\u003Cimg border=\"0\" data-original-height=\"768\" data-original-width=\"1366\" height=\"360\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/b\/R29vZ2xl\/AVvXsEg3cF0CXYwDTn5utQSKfduKeKqL-Nic3ceJSYgLO0KOXGPotkX7-3X6Ekf5dmBYw6_JaYylEkn4S3wplZQ175tuh-sNbvy70EFSvKiQRDIvEcT5UhE7Co99X6PDU_j05FwA845jujHoZtRWCg3fTf2DyBqizgoTsGPFdVdWUnFhsXfE2CqAVODLuxDuFg\/w640-h360\/Screenshot%20(226).png\" width=\"640\" \/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E469 subjects were included of 75 to 85 years old. These participants were involved in\u0026nbsp; follow-up period of 5.1 years. These patients were involved in leisure activities of , reading, playing board games, playing musical instruments, and dancing, along with physical activities. Participants who were involved in leisure activities were associated with a reduced risk of dementia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E7528 participants of the Rotterdam study aged 55-106 years.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;474 cases of dementia were detected, giving an overall prevalence of 6.3%.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAlzheimer's disease was the main subdiagnosis (339 cases; 72%).\u0026nbsp; The relative proportion of vascular dementia (76 cases; 16%), Parkinson's disease dementia (30; 6%), and other dementias (24; 5%) decreased with age.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; Pathogenesis of vascular dementia is such that a Small vessel disease, thromboembolism or hypoperfusion of the brain leads to reduced cerebral blood flow leading to hypoxia, oxidative stress, inflammation further leading to white matter damage such as demyelination, neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation which eventually leads to cognitive decline, vascular dementia.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; If the patient has an abrupt onset of symptoms, fluctuating memory, focal neurological symptoms or signs you give 2 points. For patients with hypertension, depression, personality changes, associated atherosclerosis 1 point is given.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA score less than 4 is indicative of Alzheimer's dementia\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E7 or more is indivative or vascular dementia. The functional benefits and neuroprotective effects of propentofylline (PPF) stem from its interference with these overlapping pathways of neurodegeneration.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both;
